name: Vivian Lark
equipment: A man's grey cardigan, two cotton dresses, a headscarf and dark glasses (Dot Pell's wardrobe)
The silver lamé premiere gown, at the studio wardrobe department, waiting
Derringer, 2 rounds loaded, in her handbag, bought on Main Street on 15 September
Switchblade, in her stocking top or her coat pocket
A tin box with her own lipstick, her mother's wedding ring and a photograph of her parents in front of a derrick in Taft, 1925
A script of The Gilded Hour, annotated in pencil
Her savings in cash, $1,140 at the start, now much less, in a cold-cream jar
features: Plain Dealing (Small-Town origin: +2 Wisdom, +1 Constitution. Once per long rest, an Insight check to tell whether someone is lying is made with advantage, and on a success she also learns whether the lie protects the liar or someone else. Working people start one step friendlier toward her)

The Long Con (two prepared covers: Dot Pell, the girl she used to be, vouched for by Mrs. Sloane; and Mrs. Ruth Calder, a widow from Bakersfield, vouched for by Mags Fennimore. In cover she has advantage on Deception, Performance and Persuasion to keep it up, and casual checks against it succeed without a roll)

Cheap Shot (once per turn, 2d6 extra damage to a creature she hits with a finesse Melee weapon or a Sidearm, if she has advantage, if another enemy of the target is within 5 ft of it, or if it believed a lie she told it within the last minute)
Quick Hands (bonus action on her turn: Dash, Disengage or Hide, or one Sleight of Hand check to lift, plant or palm something)
Racket: Roper (anyone she has talked to for ten minutes treats her as a friend until given a reason not to, and will do her a favour that costs them nothing without a check)
Back Door of Every Club (Nightclub Singer background: she can walk in the stage door of any club in town, and bartenders, cigarette girls and musicians tell her who was there last night and who paid)

personality.traits: I'm funny when I'm frightened and I'm frightened most of the time now. I learn everyone's lines, including yours. I always know where the exit is.
personality.ideals: I'm done being handed across tables. If I'm going to be looked at, I'll say what I'm looked at for.
personality.bonds: Abel Kurland, who read my scenes with me at night and told me I was an actress. Mags Fennimore, who took me in when I was eighteen. My mother, who died in Taft thinking I was going to be a star.
personality.flaws: I would rather burn the whole town down in public than win quietly, and I know it, and I can't stop.

appearance: Twenty-four, dark-haired, wide-mouthed, serious grey eyes and a way of looking slightly past you as if someone behind you had said something she doesn't believe. On screen she glows; off it, in a man's cardigan and a headscarf, she is a pretty girl from an oil town nobody looks at twice, which is the point.
backstory: Dorothy Ann Pell was born in Taft in 1923; her father died in a derrick fire when she was six and her mother took in washing. She came to Los Angeles at eighteen on the bus with forty dollars, boarded with Mags Fennimore at the beach, sang at clubs, and was signed by Castellane at twenty and renamed in an afternoon. Seven pictures; The Gilded Hour is her first lead. Harlan Shay has sent her to the Sirocco for dinners with important men since the spring. On 13 September she heard Wendell Haig say that Councilman Mabry had been 'taken care of', opened Royce Ambler's safe with the combination she had watched him use, and took his green ledger and his negatives.

dmNotes.roleplaying: Vivian is the missing actress and, once found at the end of kl-scenario-001, the campaign's heart. She is not a damsel and not a femme fatale; she is a working actress with a plan, a temper and a grief. She keeps the green ledger hidden in the carousel horse until the party has earned it (kl-scenario-003), helps them read the negatives and the lot, and in kl-scenario-004 decides to read the ledger into the premiere's radio microphone. Use her as a companion who argues: she wants the public truth, and she is usually braver than is sensible.
dmNotes.voice: Two voices: the studio one, low and smooth and finished, which she uses on men in dinner jackets; and Dot's, Kern County flat, quick and wry, which she uses on people she trusts. The party will know they have been trusted when she switches.
dmNotes.motivations: Primary: finish Haig and Ambler, in public, under her own name. Secondary: find out who killed Abel, and make them say it. Tertiary: survive, if possible; she is not sure it matters.
dmNotes.secrets: She argued with Abel on the telephone the day before he died ('Then I'll do it without you') and the answering-service operator heard it; she has not told the party and is ashamed. She also knows that Percy Ainsworth was the one who arranged her first Sirocco dinner, and she has forgiven him, mostly. She does not know Harlan Shay was at the pool, and when she learns it she will want to kill him; let the party talk her down.
dmNotes.attitude: Toward the party: wary, then loyal to the ones who were honest with her. Toward Bunny Shearer: absolute trust. Toward Percy: affection and a sharp tongue. Toward Shay: she liked him, which makes it worse. Toward Mags: she is the only person Vivian ever lets win an argument.
